metrics.name: mc_crate_deliveries_total
metrics.help: Item DELIVERIES, not items delivered: eight keys given at once count as one. "source" is key_grant, crate_grant or reward_grant. Only PHYSICAL keys go through here — granting a virtual key fires no event and only shows up as a jump in mc_crate_player_keys.

metrics.name: mc_crate_keys
metrics.help: Keys declared.

metrics.name: mc_crate_open_attempts_total
metrics.help: Opens REQUESTED, whether they completed or not. Checks the invariant attempts = opens + failures; a gap means the plugin opened a crate without going through the normal path.

metrics.name: mc_crate_open_cooldown_seconds
metrics.help: Delay imposed between two opens of the same crate.

metrics.name: mc_crate_open_cost
metrics.help: Price of an open. "currency" is the configured cost engine, which leaves the door open to multiple currencies, as with the economy module.

metrics.name: mc_crate_open_failures_total
metrics.help: Opens refused. "reason" is INFERRED from the player's state at the time of the request, since the plugin only returns a translated message: cooldown, no_key, money, cancelled, other.

metrics.name: mc_crate_opens_total
metrics.help: Opens completed, across all players.

metrics.name: mc_crate_placements_total
metrics.help: Physical crates placed in the world.

metrics.name: mc_crate_player_cooldown_seconds
metrics.help: Time REMAINING before a player can reopen a crate. Zero if they can open right away.

metrics.name: mc_crate_player_keys
metrics.help: VIRTUAL keys in stock for a connected player. Physical keys are in their inventory and are not counted here.

metrics.name: mc_crate_player_opens
metrics.help: A player's opens EVER, by crate type. Persisted by the plugin: the only metric in this module that doesn't reset to zero on restart.

metrics.name: mc_crate_player_opens_total
metrics.help: Opens completed, per player and per crate. Counts SINCE THE EXPORTER STARTED; for the all-time total, see mc_crate_player_opens, which the plugin persists.

metrics.name: mc_crate_player_reward_wins
metrics.help: How many times a player has won a given reward, ever. WITHOUT a "crate" label: the plugin indexes these wins by reward identifier ALONE, so two crates that both name a reward "diamond" share the counter. That's not a design choice, it's what the data allows.

metrics.name: mc_crate_previews_total
metrics.help: Previews opened without opening the crate: interest that doesn't convert.

metrics.name: mc_crate_reward_candidates
metrics.help: Rewards actually in play at the last draw. Lower than crate_rewards_configured when win limits or permissions removed rewards: this is what explains why a player can no longer win a reward they already got.

metrics.name: mc_crate_reward_expected_ratio
metrics.help: EXPECTED probability of a reward, between 0 and 1, normalized BY US (weight / sum of weights). Describes the draw's configuration, not the effective odds: guaranteed rewards, win limits and permissions are applied on top of it.

metrics.name: mc_crate_reward_required_keys
metrics.help: Keys required to be eligible for a reward. This is the ONLY notion of rarity the plugin has: there is no getRarity() in its API.

metrics.name: mc_crate_reward_weight
metrics.help: Raw weight of a reward in the draw. This is NOT a percentage.

metrics.name: mc_crate_reward_win_limit
metrics.help: Maximum number of times a reward can be won. NEGATIVE means unlimited: -1 is what the plugin returns, observed on its sample crates, not 0 as one might assume.

metrics.name: mc_crate_rewards_configured
metrics.help: Rewards declared on a crate. The Lite edition caps this at 5: this gauge says when that cap is hit.

metrics.name: mc_crate_rewards_total
metrics.help: Rewards actually HANDED OUT. "alternative" distinguishes the consolation reward from the drawn one.

metrics.name: mc_crate_selective_confirms_total
metrics.help: Choices confirmed in selective mode, where the player picks their reward.

metrics.name: mc_crate_types
metrics.help: Crate types declared.

collector.name: crate
collector.text:
PhoenixCrates metrics — and above all: does the randomness keep its promises? That's the one thing you can't see in-game. A player who opens a hundred crates can sense that the reward advertised at 2% never comes up, but can't prove it; neither can an admin. Two metrics settle it: 
`# OBSERVED probability over 30 days, against the CONFIGURED one sum by (crate,reward) (increase(mc_crate_rewards_total{alternative="false"`[30d])) / ignoring(reward) group_left sum by (crate) (increase(mc_crate_rewards_total{alternative="false"}[30d])) / mc_crate_reward_expected_ratio # 1.0 = matches, 0.5 = half as frequent as promised }
There is no way to measure the raw draw, which had to be learned the hard way on the server. This module originally declared a `reward_draws` counter fed by `CrateRewardSelectionEvent` — which never fires as its name suggests. The event fires BEFORE the draw, with the list of candidates and a `null` reward, to let a third-party plugin impose its own choice; only afterward, if nobody responded, does `selectByWeight` actually draw. So there's no draw outcome to listen for. The fallback is `rewards_total` filtered on `alternative="false"`: what gets handed out WITHOUT having been substituted. An acknowledged imprecision remains — win limits and permissions remove candidates before the draw, invisibly. Hence `crate_reward_candidates`, which says how many rewards were actually in play. Two regimes live in one class. The counters are fed by events and cost nothing at scrape time: they're already current. The gauges — configuration and per-player state — require walking lists, hence `#isBackground()` being true. Both mechanics live here together because they describe the same object; splitting them would force sharing crate identifiers between two classes. All handlers run at `MONITOR` and in O(1). PhoenixCrates' events fire on the main thread, in the call stack of the open itself — verified at the bytecode level. A handler that took a millisecond would take it out of the tick.
